gp.heading: Cost of Sales / Gross Profit
gp.text:
Cost of sales decreased by $186 million, or 1%, and gross profit increased by $33 million, or 4%, during fiscal 2025 as compared to fiscal 2024. The year over year decrease in cost of sales was primarily due to lower production volumes ($174 million), favorable supplier pricing adjustments including KEIPER supply agreement modifications ($70 million), favorable material economics ($31 million), favorable operating performance despite the $45 million unfavorable impact of tariffs ($27 million) and lower depreciation and amortization expense ($4 million), partially offset by the unfavorable impact of foreign currencies ($101 million) and higher restructuring-related charges ($19 million). Gross profit for fiscal 2025 was impacted by favorable commercial and supplier pricing adjustments, favorable operating performance, lower depreciation expense and the favorable impact of foreign currencies, partially offset by lower production volumes and unfavorable product mix, unfavorable material economics, net of recoveries, unfavorable net tariff impact, and higher restructuring-related charges. Refer to the segment analysis below for a discussion of segment profitability.

Cost of sales decreased by $602 million, or 4%, and gross profit decreased by $105 million, or 10%, during fiscal 2024 as compared to fiscal 2023.

These uncertainties are the result of a combination of factors including weakening consumer demand due in part to vehicle affordability, the direct and indirect impacts resulting from the imposition of U.S. and foreign tariffs, market share loss for foreign/luxury OEMs in the Asia reporting unit combined with modest expected margin declines as Adient continues to win new business with local OEMs in China, intensifying competition from Chinese imports and lower exports to China from EMEA as domestic brands expand in China and overcapacity in the EMEA reporting unit resulting in pricing pressure along with continued disruptions caused by slower electric vehicle adoption rates.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (“SG&A”)
sga.text: SG&A expenses increased by $15 million, or 3%, during fiscal 2025 as compared to fiscal 2024. The year over year increase in SG&A was primarily due to higher compensation expense including the impact of prior year austerity measures ($21 million), third-party consulting costs associated with strategic planning ($9 million), higher net engineering and other administrative spending ($8 million) and the unfavorable impact of foreign currencies ($2 million), partially offset by the higher level of gains on the sale of assets ($13 million), the non-recurrence of a prior year one-time loss on business divestiture ($8 million), lower depreciation and amortization expense ($2 million) and other non-recurring items ($2 million).

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and operating loss and other loss carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Adient records a valuation allowance that primarily represents operating and other loss carryforwards for which realization is uncertain. Management judgment is required in determining Adient's provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, and the valuation allowance recorded against Adient's net deferred tax assets.

Adient reviews the realizability of its deferred tax assets on a quarterly basis, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that a review is required. In determining the requirement for a valuation allowance, the historical and projected financial results of the legal entity or combined group recording the net deferred tax asset are considered, along with any other positive or negative evidence.

net.text: • Net loss attributable to Adient was $281 million for fiscal 2025, compared to net income attributable to Adient of $18 million for fiscal 2024. The net loss in fiscal 2025 is primarily attributable to the $333 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge recorded in the EMEA segment and the $8 million non-cash impairment on Adient’s investment in Adient Aerospace, lower overall production volumes, unfavorable material economics, net of recoveries, higher income tax expense and lower equity income, partially offset by favorable commercial and supplier pricing adjustments and favorable operating performance.

ocf.heading: Cash flows from operating activities
ocf.text:
Fiscal 2025 compared to Fiscal 2024: The decrease in cash flows from operating activities is primarily due to an increase in customer tooling and capitalized engineering spending associated with launch activity primarily in EMEA and a higher level of cash payments associated with restructuring activities.

Fiscal 2024 compared to Fiscal 2023: The decrease in cash flows from operating activities is primarily due to lower profitability driven by lower production volumes in fiscal 2024 along with unfavorable changes to working capital year over year.

gp.heading: Cost of Sales / Gross Profit
gp.text:
Cost of sales increased by $636 million, or 5%, and gross profit decreased by $3 million, less than 1%, during fiscal 2026 as compared to fiscal 2025. The year-over-year increase in cost of sales was primarily due to the impact of higher production volumes and unfavorable product mix in Americas and Asia, partially offset by lower production volumes in EMEA as a result of weak customer demand ($207 million), the unfavorable impact of foreign currencies ($275 million) and unfavorable net operating performance mainly driven by higher freight and launch costs as well as unfavorable material costs largely driven by the impact of the Middle East conflict, net of the impact of IEEPA tariff refunds ($154 million). Gross profit for fiscal 2026 was impacted by unfavorable volume and unfavorable product mix, partially offset by net operating performance including the impact of favorable commercial actions and favorable material costs and the favorable impact of foreign currencies.

Cost of sales decreased by $186 million, or 1%, and gross profit increased by $33 million, or 4%, during fiscal 2025 as compared to fiscal 2024.

capex.heading: Capital expenditures
capex.text:

Fiscal 2025 compared to Fiscal 2024: Lower capital expenditures in fiscal 2025 were due primarily to timing of program spend on product launches in Americas and Asia.

Net sales decreased by $153 million, or 1%, during fiscal 2025 as compared to fiscal 2024 due to lower overall production volumes in EMEA as a result of weak customer demand, net of higher production volumes in Americas and Asia ($225 million) and unfavorable material economics recoveries ($59 million), partially offset by the favorable impact of foreign currencies ($104 million) and favorable commercial pricing adjustments which includes $28 million related to tariff recoveries ($27 million).

intro.text: Adient plc (“Adient”) is a global leader in the automotive seating supply industry with leading market positions in the Americas, Europe and Asia and maintains longstanding relationships with the largest global automotive original equipment manufacturers (“OEMs”). Adient's proprietary technologies extend into virtually every area of automotive seating solutions, including complete seating systems, frames, mechanisms, foam, head restraints, armrests and trim covers. Adient is a global seat supplier with the capability to design, develop, engineer, manufacture, and deliver complete seat systems and components in every major automotive producing region in the world.

The financial projections considered the impact of the various issues causing uncertainty in the automotive industry such as consumer demand volatility due in part to vehicle affordability and high interest rate environment, the direct and indirect impacts resulting from the imposition of U.S. and foreign tariffs including onshoring opportunities in the U.S., market share loss in China for foreign/luxury OEMs in the Asia reporting unit combined with modest margin declines as Adient continues to win new business with local OEMs in China, lower exports from Asia due to the Middle East conflict, continued volatility caused by slower electric vehicle global adoption rates, higher input costs such as energy and freight resulting from conflicts in the Middle East and other parts of the world, intensifying global competition from Chinese exports, lower exports to China from EMEA as domestic brands expand in China and overcapacity in the EMEA reporting unit resulting in pricing pressure.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (“SG&A”)
sga.text:
SG&A increased by $33 million, or 6%, during fiscal 2026 as compared to fiscal 2025 due to higher compensation expense including equity and performance-based incentive compensation costs ($35 million), lower amounts of gains on sales of facilities in the current year ($21 million) and the unfavorable impact of foreign currencies ($16 million), partially offset by lower net engineering and other administrative spending ($28 million) and third-party consulting costs associated with strategic planning in the previous year and other non-recurring items ($11 million).

SG&A expenses increased by $15 million, or 3%, during fiscal 2025 as compared to fiscal 2024. The year over year increase in SG&A was primarily due to higher compensation expense including the impact of austerity measures in fiscal 2024 ($21 million), third-party consulting costs associated with strategic planning ($9 million), higher net engineering and other administrative spending ($8 million) and the unfavorable impact of foreign currencies ($2 million), partially offset by the higher level of gains on the sale of assets ($13 million), the non-recurrence of a one-time loss on business divestiture in fiscal 2024 ($8 million), lower depreciation and amortization expense ($2 million) and other non-recurring items ($2 million).

Refer to the segment analysis below for a discussion of segment profitability.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and operating loss and other loss carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Adient records a valuation allowance that primarily represents operating and other loss carryforwards for which realization is uncertain. Management judgment is required in determining Adient's provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, and the valuation allowance recorded against Adient's net deferred tax assets.

Adient reviews the realizability of its deferred tax assets on a quarterly basis, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that a review is required. In determining the requirement for a valuation allowance, the historical and projected financial results of the legal entity or combined group recording the net deferred tax asset are considered, along with any other positive or negative evidence.

net.text: Net loss attributable to Adient was $281 million during fiscal 2025, compared to net income attributable to Adient of $18 million during fiscal 2024. The net loss in fiscal 2025 is primarily attributable to the $333 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge recorded in the EMEA segment and the $8 million non-cash impairment on its investment in Adient Aerospace, lower overall production volumes, unfavorable material economics, net of recoveries, higher income tax expense, lower equity income due to the unfavorable impact of the KEIPER supply agreement modifications, higher SG&A expenses mainly driven by third-party consulting costs associated with strategic planning and higher income attributable to noncontrolling interests, partially offset by favorable commercial and supplier pricing adjustments, favorable operating performance and lower pension expense.

ocf.text: Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025: The increase in cash flows from operating activities in fiscal 2026 is primarily due to higher levels of customer tooling collections and the favorable impact from IEEPA refunds received in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, partially offset by a decrease in accrued liabilities resulting from the payment of indirect taxes.

da.text: Adient evaluates the performance of its reportable segments using an adjusted EBITDA metric defined as income (loss) before income taxes and noncontrolling interests, excluding net financing charges, restructuring and impairment costs, restructuring-related costs, net mark-to-market adjustments on pension plans, transaction gains/losses, purchase accounting amortization, depreciation, stock-based compensation and other non-recurring items (“Adjusted EBITDA”). Also, certain corporate-related costs are not allocated to the segments. The reportable segments are consistent with how management views the markets served by Adient and reflect the financial information that is reviewed by its chief operating decision maker. Refer to Note 17, “Segment Information,” of the notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information on Adient's reportable segments.

sbc.text: Adient evaluates the performance of its reportable segments using an adjusted EBITDA metric defined as income (loss) before income taxes and noncontrolling interests, excluding net financing charges, restructuring and impairment costs, restructuring-related costs, net mark-to-market adjustments on pension plans, transaction gains/losses, purchase accounting amortization, depreciation, stock-based compensation and other non-recurring items (“Adjusted EBITDA”). Also, certain corporate-related costs are not allocated to the segments. The reportable segments are consistent with how management views the markets served by Adient and reflect the financial information that is reviewed by its chief operating decision maker. Refer to Note 17, “Segment Information,” of the notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information on Adient's reportable segments.

wc.heading: Working capital
wc.text: Working capital decreased by $129 million primarily due to an increase in accounts payable resulting from higher levels of production activities and a decrease in cash and cash equivalents, partially offset by an increase in accounts receivable, a decrease in accrued liabilities resulting from the payment of indirect taxes, as well as a decrease in other current liabilities.

capex.heading: Capital expenditures
capex.text:
Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025: Higher capital expenditures in fiscal 2026 were driven by higher levels of investments in artificial intelligence (“AI”), automation and innovation as well as expenditures related to new and replacement programs. Investments in AI, automation and innovation are expected to continue for the foreseeable future.

Fiscal 2025 compared to Fiscal 2024: Lower capital expenditures in fiscal 2025 were due primarily to timing of program spend on product launches in Americas and Asia.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Net sales increased by $633 million, or 4%, during fiscal 2026 as compared to fiscal 2025 due to the favorable impact of foreign currencies ($292 million), higher production volumes in Americas and Asia, partially offset by lower production volumes in EMEA as a result of weak customer demand ($135 million) and the net favorable impact of commercial pricing adjustments, net of the reduction in net sales resulting from amounts expected to be passed on to Adient's customers related to IEEPA tariff refunds ($206 million).

Net sales decreased by $153 million, or 1%, during fiscal 2025 as compared to fiscal 2024 due to lower overall production volumes in EMEA as a result of weak customer demand, net of higher production volumes in Americas and Asia ($225 million) and unfavorable material economics recoveries ($59 million), partially offset by the favorable impact of foreign currencies ($104 million) and favorable commercial pricing adjustments which includes $28 million related to tariff recoveries ($27 million).

Refer to the segment analysis below for a discussion of segment net sales.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

Automotive production and sales are highly cyclical and depend on general economic conditions and other factors, including consumer spending and preferences.

Although Adient has no operations in the Middle East or Ukraine and its operation in Russia has since been disposed, certain of its suppliers as well as customers depend on commodities and other material supplies that originate in the Middle East, Ukraine or Russia.
Adient has also experienced constrained labor availability which has resulted in wage inflationary pressures, both internally and at key vendors.
Additionally, consolidation in the automotive industry may lead to decreased product purchases from Adient.

Adient relies upon the capacity, reliability and security of its IT and data security infrastructure, as well as its ability to expand and continually update this infrastructure in response to the changing needs of its business.

Adient’s operations depend on the availability, integrity and resilience of IT and operational technology systems used in its manufacturing, engineering, logistics and administrative activities, as well as interconnected systems and critical technology services operated by its customers, suppliers, sub-suppliers, cloud and housing providers, software and services providers, consultants and other third parties.
Adient's business success depends on attracting and retaining qualified personnel.

Adient is responsible for managing its supply chain, including suppliers that may be the sole sources of products that Adient requires, which Adient's customers direct Adient to use or which have unique capabilities that would make it difficult and/or expensive to re-source.
Adient's ability to pay dividends will depend on its ongoing ability to generate cash from operations and access capital markets.

Any future cash dividends will be at the discretion of the Board of Directors and will depend upon Adient's financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, alternative uses of capital and other factors the Board of Directors may consider at its discretion.

The number of ordinary shares repurchased, if any, and the timing of repurchases will depend on a number of factors, including share price, trading volume and general market conditions, as well as on working capital requirements, general business conditions and other factors.
Adient's principal sources of liquidity are cash flows from operating activities, the revolving credit facility and other debt issuances, and existing cash balances.
